title: Client DAO-ACK fingerprint is raw wire plus 40-byte cap
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: robustness

ShortAddressAssignmentClient::apply_dao_ack() stores the entire received DAO-ACK (MAX_ACK_WIRE=40) and treats any byte difference at the same DAOSequence as conflicting DAO-ACK for one sequence.

one_assignment_option() already ignores Pad1 and non-252 options, and DaoAck::from_bytes() does not require reserved flag bits to be zero. Semantically identical ACKs that add Pad1/PadN, an extra ignored option, or reserved flag bits therefore parse to the same AddressAssignmentAck but fail the raw-wire compare after the first ACK was accepted.

MAX_ACK_WIRE=40 is also too tight: DAO-ACK with DODAGID is 20+16=36 bytes, leaving 4 bytes of slack. A valid first ACK at 41 bytes (DODAGID form plus modest padding) is parsed, then rejected with DAO-ACK exceeds stored fingerprint and never installed.

Python fingerprints ack.to_bytes() (canonical re-encode) with no size cap, so padded retransmissions are accepted there and rejected or conflicted here. Fix: fingerprint the parsed assignment fields (and maybe canonical encoding), not the raw buffer; drop or raise the 40-byte cap to the LoRa frame limit.
